text: You're looking at a country that survived about 1700 years right in the middle of Italy.
It even turned down free land from Napoleon.
This is San Marino, just 61 square kilometers, about half the size of Paris.
And Italy has two countries inside it.
The other is the Vatican, the smallest on Earth.
So how does something this tiny stay free, surrounded on every side?
The story goes, a stonemason named Marinus climbed this mountain and started a tiny community.
Fifteen centuries later, Napoleon is marching through Italy. He likes San Marino and offers to make it bigger.
Their leaders reason? Wars end, but neighbors remain. And it's believed that saved them.
When Napoleon fell, they had no land to give back.
Then, in 1849, they hid Garibaldi, a hero of Italy's unification from an Austrian army.
So when Italy came together, San Marino was allowed to stay free.
The best way to survive next to a giant is to never want its land.
They even made Abraham Lincoln an honorary citizen in 1861.
